newsitem.title: USA: GOOD WEATHER FOR U.S. COTTON STATES AIDS GROWTH.
newsitem.headline: GOOD WEATHER FOR U.S. COTTON STATES AIDS GROWTH.

text.p: Mixed weather reports from U.S. cotton producer states this week showed scattered, late week rains help improve development of crops, according to reports from the National Agricultural Statistics Service. Dry conditions in some states required irrigation, but most reports show crop progress on par with last year. Insect reports have increased slightly, and growers continue to spray fields.

MISSISSIPPI - According to the Mississippi Agricultural Statistics Service, there were 2.5 days suitable for fieldwork for the week ending August 10, 1997. Soil moisture conditions were rated 39 percent surplus, 46 percent adequate, ten percent short and five percent very short. Good weather conditions have helped the cotton to make up for lost time, according to county extension officials. Insect pressure has been light to this point. Boll weevil eradication got underway with no problems reported.

Setting bolls rated 99 percent this week versus 95 percent last week, 100 percent last year and 98 percent on a five year average. Bolls opening rated seven percent this week, two percent last week, ten percent last year, and four percent on average. Crop conditions were rated ten percent excellent, 63 percent good, 23 percent fair, and four percent poor.

LOUISIANA - According to Louisiana state reports, there were 5.5 days suitable for fieldwork last week. Soil moisture rated ten percent surplus, 53 percent adequate, 27 percent short, and ten percent very short. Crop conditions rated six percent excellent, 44 percent good, 36 percent fair, ten percent poor, and four percent very poor.

Setting bolls rated 100 percent this week, versus 96 percent last week, 100 percent last year, and 100 percent on a five year average. No bolls were open yet versus ten percent last year and seven percent on average.
Irrigation was active in drier areas this week, according to county officials. Cotton insect pressure was reported to be fairly light.

GEORGIA - It was another week of scattered rainfall throughout the state, according to the Georgia Agricultural Statistics Service. The moisture was generally adequate for crop development and interfered little with field work. Generally, crops are in fair to mostly good condition and little changed from last week.

Pressure from worms is intensifying and spraying is active. Insect control is now increasing in the northern cotton fields with reports of heavy infestations continuing in many southern regions. Cotton development is about a week behind normal. County extension officials reported 6.0 days suitable for fieldwork during the week.

Soil moisture rated four percent surplus, 73 percent adequate, 21 percent short, and two percent very short. Setting bolls rated 94 percent this week versus 90 percent last week, 99 percent last year and 99 percent for the five year average. Crop conditions rated 12 percent excellent, 59 percent good, 25 percent fair, and four percent poor.

TEXAS - Late week rains in the Plains were very beneficial, however cooler temperatures limited progress. Some growth regulators had been applied in scattered fields in North Central areas. Insect activity has increased in many fields. Early week hot temperatures had bolls opening rapidly in the Blacklands and Central Texas.

Harvest continued in the Coastal Bend and Rio Grande Valley, but late week rain showers slowed progress. Statewide cotton condition was rated at 71 percent of normal compared with 62 percent last year.

Crop conditions rated eight percent excellent, 42 percent good, 34 percent fair, and 14 percent poor. Setting bolls rated 83 percent this week versus 71 percent last week, 89 percent last year, and 74 percent for the five year average. Bolls opening rated 11 percent this week versus seven percent last week, 17 percent last year and 14 percent on average.
One percent of the cotton crop is harvested according to state reports. This compares with one percent last week, six percent last year, and five percent on average.

CALIFORNIA - Field activities progressed normally under clear skies in most areas of the state, according to the California Agricultural Statistics Service. Cotton was blooming and setting bolls in most fields, and bolls were beginning to open in the southern San Joaquin Valley. Growers continued to spray for aphids, lygus, mites, whiteflies, worms and weeds.

ARIZONA - Turbulent weather with heavy rains, high winds and hail was reported across the state late last week. The clouds and rainfall kept temperatures well below normal for many areas including the central and southern deserts. The monsoonal flow is expected to taper off somewhat this week as wind flows switch to a more westerly direction.

Cotton continues to progress well. Latest reports indicate that crop conditions changed little from last week. Current ratings are 30 percent excellent, 60 percent good, and ten percent fair. Virtually all Arizona cotton is setting bolls and approximately 25 to 30 percent is opening bolls.

There were some reports that hail and high winds inflicted damage on some fields in Pima county. In the southwestern counties the heat and humidity are slowing development somewhat. Also, there were reports of Lygus damage in the southwest. Despite these reports the overall cotton crop continues to look exceptionally well for this time of year. ((Eileen Houlihan, New York Commodity Desk, 212-859-1640))
